lines.text: When a honeybee stings your skin, what microscopic war explodes inside your bloodstream?
The bee's barbed stinger tears out of its abdomen, continuing to pump venom automatically for minutes.
The venom contains melittin, a powerful peptide that literally punches holes through cell membranes.
Pain receptors fire emergency alarms to your spinal cord while mast cells release waves of histamine.
Blood vessels dilate to rush white blood cells to the scene, causing rapid swelling and fiery redness.
White blood cells gobble up venom fragments over three days until the swelling recedes.
Scrape the stinger off immediately with a credit card to stop the venom pump early.
